title.en: Seeing Off Yuan the Second on a Mission to Anxi

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource.

basis.en: Tang dynasty poem; the author died in 761.

note.en: Set to music soon after it was written, it became the standard parting song of the Tang, sung with lines repeated as the Three Refrains of Yang Pass, 阳关三叠. Willow branches were broken off and given at partings, and the rain has washed them green. Everything in the poem is about a small delay: one more cup before the road begins.
note.zh: 这首诗写成后不久就被谱成乐曲，成了唐代通行的送别歌，叠唱而成《阳关三叠》。古人折柳送别，一场朝雨把柳色洗得青青。整首诗都在写一次小小的拖延：上路之前，再喝一杯。

excerpt.orig: 勸君更盡一杯酒，西出陽關無故人。
excerpt.en: I urge you, drink one more cup of wine: / west of Yang Pass you will have no old friends.
excerpt.zh: 劝君更尽一杯酒，西出阳关无故人。

gloss.en: Weicheng, the old Qin capital Xianyang, on the Wei River north-west of Chang’an, where travellers going west were seen off.
gloss.zh: 渭城：即秦都咸阳故城，在长安西北、渭水北岸，是西行送别之地。

gloss.en: To moisten, to damp down (the dust).
Willows were the emblem of parting: 柳 sounds like 留, ‘stay’, and a willow sprig was broken off for the traveller.
gloss.zh: 柳与“留”谐音，古人有折柳送别的习俗。

gloss.en: Yang Pass, south-west of Dunhuang, a gate to the western regions. Anxi, Yuan’s destination, was the Protectorate seated at Kucha, far beyond it.
gloss.zh: 阳关：在今甘肃敦煌西南，是通往西域的要道。安西：唐安西都护府，治所在龟兹（今新疆库车）。
